newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end sharply higher.

text.p: Swiss shares closed sharply higher on Thursday, powered by firmer U.S. financial markets, a strong dollar and positive company results, dealers said.

Worries that U.S. interest rates might rise cooled down after the release of the Federal Reserve' latest Beige Book report on the U.S. economy, which was seen as confirming marklet forecasts for a steady economy and rates.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) advanced 1.89 percent or 110.0 points to close at 5,922.1 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 1.66 percent or 61.58 points to 3,768.37.
Swiss shares also rose because of derivatives-related trading and technical factors, one dealer said.
Shares of volume-leader CS Group rose 3.75 percent or 7.50 francs to 207.50.
Dealers said the title was helped by a renewed bout of rumours that were dismissed last month about some kind of stronger alliance or merger with insurer Winterthur.
UBS bearer shares, which were under pressure for two days after half-year figures on Tuesday, rose 36 francs to 1,660.
Novartis closed 40 francs higher at 2,392 francs.
Swiss shares of electrical engineer ABB, which is also traded in Sweden, advanced 2.35 percent or 52 francs to 2,266 after publishing first-half results.
Dealers said group net profit growth was below expectations at only two percent. But the share drew strength from positive company prospects for the seocnd half and next year.
Watchmaker SMH and cement maker Holderbank rose on the back of the stronger dollar.
SMH gained 39 francs to 915. Holderbank advance 1.8 percent or 25 dollars to 1,411.
Roche gained 230 francs to end at 14.650.
